title: Four Final Forms Before the Verbs

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write બ once from memory. Put it away after one comparison. Today adds one new sound and one new shape: ga.
Keep ગ (ga) visible. Circle the rounded left body to the lower left. Lift once, descend the separate right spine, and turn through its lower foot.
Finger-trace ગ (ga) once, then air-trace it once. Notice rounded body, separate right spine, lower foot; one pen lift.
Copy visible ગ (ga) once. Compare only the body and spine; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write ga once. Uncover ગ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write ga from memory.

feedback.correct: ગ — the rounded body and separate spine are intact.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at ગ, hide it, and repair only the differing landmark.

segments.text: Name the sound, the two main landmarks, and the pen-lift count.
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Read ગ (ga) once, then write independent અ once from memory. Say “standing alone,” then put both away. The next independent vowel has its own whole-letter form.
Keep એ visible. Circle the left bowl and continue through the lower body and small right arch. Lift once for the full-height right stem and foot. Lift again and sweep the high arc from left to right.
Finger-trace એ once, then air-trace it once. Notice joined body, separate stem, high arc; two pen lifts.
Copy visible એ once. Compare only the separate stem and high arc; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write independent e once. Uncover એ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write independent e from memory.

feedback.correct: એ — the body, stem, and high arc are intact.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at એ, hide it, and repair only the differing landmark.

segments.text: Say why this is a whole vowel letter rather than a mark attached to a consonant.
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write unaspirated ક once. Say ka. Add a clear puff of air aloud for kha, then put the old shape away.
Keep ખ (kha) visible. Descend through the joined left lobe and curl right through the middle. Lift once, descend the separate right spine, and turn through its lower foot.
Finger-trace ખ (kha) once, then air-trace it once. Notice left lobe, inner curl, separate spine; one pen lift.
Copy visible ખ (kha) once. Compare only the inner curl and right spine; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write kha once. Uncover ખ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write aspirated kha from memory.

feedback.correct: ખ — the lobe, curl, and separate spine are intact.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at ખ, hide it, and repair only the differing landmark.

segments.text: Read ક ખ aloud and keep unaspirated ka apart from aspirated kha.
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — meet one form until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write attached short-u sign ુ once and say “needs a consonant.” Put it away. The same vowel standing alone needs a whole letter.
Keep ઉ visible. Circle the small upper bowl to the middle cusp. Continue around the broad lower bowl, then climb the tall outer curve and finish at the upper right without lifting.
Finger-trace ઉ once, then air-trace it once. Notice upper bowl, middle cusp, lower bowl, outer return; no pen lift.
Copy visible ઉ once. Compare only the two bowls and outer return; repair one landmark if needed.
Hide the model and write independent u once. Uncover ઉ, compare, and stop after one repair.

segments.prompt: Hide the model and write independent short u from memory.

feedback.correct: ઉ — the two bowls and tall outer return are intact.
feedback.incorrect: Look once at ઉ, hide it, and repair only the differing landmark.

segments.text: Point to the whole vowel in ઉ (u) ુ, then point to the attached sign.
Sources: Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice and the Unicode Gujarati chart.

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Keep the four cards visible. Point as you say ga, independent e, aspirated kha, and independent short u.
Read the row once from left to right. Name એ and ઉ as independent vowels. Record a reading score out of four.

segments.prompt: Read these four forms aloud in order: ગ (ga) એ ખ (kha) ઉ.
acceptedResponses: ga; independent e; aspirated kha; independent short u

feedback.incorrect: Name only the missed form, compare one landmark, then read the row again.

segments.text: Cover every model. Write the four cues in order. Record a separate writing score out of four; a reading point cannot replace a written form. Aim for 4/4 in each column, with one focused repair allowed.

segments.prompt: Cover every model. Write from these cues: ga, independent e, aspirated kha, independent short u.

feedback.correct: The four forms returned without a visible model.
feedback.incorrect: Uncover only the missed form, repair one landmark, cover it, and retry once.
